key_insight: SNOW is a fast, differentiable neural surrogate that reproduces global MHD solar wind evolution from 20 to 240 Rs while preserving key plasma and magnetic-field structures.
engineering_relevance: It enables near-real-time, repeated heliospheric simulations on a single GPU, making global solar-wind modeling far more practical for forecasting and sensitivity studies.
method: Combines rotational ballistic approximation with a spherical harmonic neural operator.
Uses causal radial context to autoregressively advance all eight MHD variables shell by shell.
Trained on AWSoM solar-cycle simulations and rolled out across the full 3D domain.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on AWSoM simulations spanning a solar cycle and remained stable through complete rollouts, while matching large-scale flow, magnetic polarity, divergence, and induction diagnostics.
watch_item: Because the surrogate is trained on AWSoM-based data and uses autoregressive shell propagation, generalization beyond the training regime and error accumulation over long rollouts need careful validation.
paper_title: Fast and Differentiable MHD Surrogate for Solar Wind using Neural Operator
